title: His record collection and bootlegs
summary: He keeps only odds and ends at home; a friend has nearly all his recordings, many from bootleg sources.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You don't necessarily keep much of a record collection in the house, do you?
No, I just have odds and ends.
Yeah. Do you have everything that you recorded commercially? You don't, do you?
I don't, no. But a friend of mine has just about everything.
And he's still picking up stuff. He finds it everywhere in the world, you know. Through bootleg operations. (Inaudible.)
Oh, yeah. As you say, there's probably more things recorded on bootleg than ever recorded commercially in total.
